info.title: Adaptive Learning API
info.description: Operational endpoints plus the Phase 1 learning MVP for AWS SOA-C03.

get.description:
Returns `200` when the database is reachable and `503` when it is not, so a
load balancer can stop routing to an instance whose dependency is down.

503.description: Service is running but the database is unavailable

get.summary: Internal calibration summary for a model version.
get.description:
Analytics only: returns aggregate metrics, never per-user data. Disabled
outside local/test by default, and when enabled outside local/test it
requires an explicit `X-Internal-Token`. A learner token alone is never
enough, so this is not part of the learner-facing surface.

parameters.name: model_version
parameters.description: Model version to evaluate. Defaults to the current model.

parameters.name: bucket_count
parameters.description: Number of calibration buckets (1-20). Defaults to 5.

get.description:
The document is the source of truth for the TypeScript client. Regenerate it
with `cargo run -p adaptive-learn-api --bin export-openapi` or the web
`pnpm generate:api` script.

get.summary: Lists certifications, versions, domains, and authored tasks.
Returns the pre-quiz learning content for a certification domain.
get.description:
This is the Knowledge Map curriculum: modules, knowledge nodes, and
progressive reveals. It is a discovery mechanic, not a scored assessment, so
it is deliberately separate from mission issuance and scoring. Learning
content requires an authenticated account.

404.description: No learning content for this domain

get.summary: Lists the practice tests (exam simulations) for a certification.
Returns learner-safe practice-test content, before submission.
get.description: Canonical answers, per-choice feedback, and scored flags are never included.

post.summary: Scores and reviews a complete practice-test attempt.
post.description:
The whole attempt is submitted at once; the response reveals canonical
answers, explanations, and per-choice feedback. The raw practice score is
not an official scaled score.

post.summary: Debits Bits for one Cyber Defense control upgrade.
post.description:
The wallet is taken from the verified token, so an anonymous caller is
rejected: spending is an account-scoped, server-authoritative action. The
client sends the action's primitives and an idempotency `event_id`; the
server derives the cost and settles the debit exactly once.

409.description: Insufficient Bits, an out-of-sequence upgrade level, or a reused idempotency key

post.summary: Completes a learning-node Daily Mission item from discovery progress.

get.summary: Reviews the questions and answers of a Daily Mission item.
get.description:
Available after the item's practice mission completes, so a learner can
revisit the material without redoing it. It never creates evidence.

post.summary: Starts the mission for one Daily Mission practice item.

400.description: Item is completed on the knowledge map

get.summary: Returns safe application account data for the authenticated learner.
get.description:
Used to confirm server-side auth and to power the account UI. It never
returns tokens, secrets, or provider internals. The account-wide study streak
and study settings are bundled here so the Track Hub needs no extra request;
a query failure returns neutral values and never fails authentication.

put.description:
Settings are preferences only: they never affect scoring, evidence, concept
state, or rewards.

post.summary: Issues a mission for a quiz mode.
post.description:
Authenticated callers get a user-owned mission. Anonymous callers may issue
public demo task-practice missions only.

post.summary: Scores one attempt and returns immediate feedback.

409.description: Mission completed, content version mismatch, or stale mission content (`mission_content_stale`)

post.summary: Marks a mission completed for its owner.

get.summary: Returns a read-only review of a completed mission.
get.description:
Canonical answers are included only after completion, so in-progress work
never leaks answers. Review never creates evidence or changes scores.

post.summary: Reconciles a batch of attempts, re-scoring each against canonical content.
post.description:
The authenticated user is inferred from the bearer token; ownership of every
referenced mission is checked server-side. Anonymous demo events are
accepted for demo missions but never settle Bits.

post.summary: Returns today's immutable Daily Mission, generating it once if needed.
post.description:
The plan never changes after creation, and generation is optional: if
adaptive planning fails, a standard non-adaptive plan is persisted instead.

get.summary: Returns a learner's persisted Knowledge Map discovery progress for a track.
get.description:
This is an enhancement, not a prerequisite: the Knowledge Map renders from
local progress immediately and merges this response asynchronously. It is raw
monotonic discovery data and never scored knowledge evidence.

get.summary: Returns every learning domain for a track in one response.
get.description:
The Track Hub renders one track-wide Knowledge Map, so this avoids a request
per domain. It is authored content only: no scored answers, no learner state.

get.summary: Returns the aggregate Knowledge Signal for a track.
get.description:
One request covers every domain and node. Coarse semantic states only: no raw
model probabilities, percentages, or pass estimates. This is an enhancement:
if it fails, the client renders the normal Knowledge Map from discovery
progress and omits the adaptive decoration.

post.summary: Returns a best-effort next-action recommendation for a learning track.
post.description:
This is an optional, explainable layer over the derived concept state. It
never gates the dashboard, knowledge maps, or quizzes, and it never creates
learning evidence. Requires an authenticated account.

Telemetry is auxiliary: the request succeeds even when the write fails, so it
can never block the learner.

post.summary: Builds an optional adaptive study session for a learning track.
post.description:
Session planning is optional and best-effort: the client falls back to a
standard non-adaptive session when this fails. The server selects all
practice questions. Requires an authenticated account.

get.summary: Returns the authenticated user's settled Bits balance.
get.description:
The wallet is identified by the verified token, never by a query parameter,
so a caller can only read their own balance.

oneOf.description: Browser-executed Python test counts for a `python_code` question.

AssessmentMode.description:
How an attempt measures knowledge.

The first four are the base evidence modes from `docs/06-learning-engine.md`.
The remaining two are explicit Phase 1 subtypes used by tactile
interactions; they are still treated as evidence modes, not proven
independent latent abilities.

AuxiliaryEventRequest.description: One auxiliary recommendation lifecycle event sent in a sync batch.

oneOf.description: Planner action the recommendation had, when known.

event_id.description: Stable client-generated id, used to make retried telemetry idempotent.

CalibrationBucketDto.description: One calibration bucket in an internal evaluation summary.

mean_observed.description: Mean observed score in the bucket.

mean_prediction.description: Mean predicted probability in the bucket.

oneOf.description: Correct item-to-category placements.
Correct order of item ids.
Correct directed relationships.
Correct piece placed in each slot.

oneOf.description: Evidence source ids that are relevant to the question.

relevant_ids.description: Relevant evidence ids. Every other candidate is a false positive.

oneOf.description: Element ids that are faulty.
Correct value id for each slot id.
Correct decisions for a diagnosis/remediation scenario.

correct_choice_ids.description: Step id to the choice ids that are correct at that step.

expected_path.description: The intended ordered choice ids from the start step.

oneOf.description: Correct decisions for an authored decision chain.

correct_choice_ids.description: Step id to the choice ids that are correct at that step.

expected_path.description: The intended ordered choice ids from the start step.

oneOf.description: Correct component assignment for each role.
Correct tolerant region for each placed item.

regions.description: Item id to its canonical region.

oneOf.description: Correct token for each ordered slot.
Accepted typed answers for each inline blank.

answers.description: Slot id to the authored accepted answers.

oneOf.description: The single correct choice id.
The exact set of correct choice ids.

choice_ids.description: Correct choice ids; order is not significant.

oneOf.description:
Data-driven tests the browser executes against the learner's program.

These are the canonical behavioral specification. They are inspectable
because execution happens client-side, so they must not encode secrets.

tests.description: Authored tests, run in declaration order.

CanonicalAnswer.description: The canonical answer for a question.

CertificationDto.description: A certification with its versioned blueprints.

concepts.description:
Learner-facing knowledge concepts referenced by this version.

Mission payloads carry only concept ids; the catalog supplies the names so
summaries never have to render a raw identifier.

CodeAnnotation.description: A clickable region inside a `code_file` reveal.

explanation.description: Explanation revealed when the region is clicked.

id.description: Stable annotation identifier, also the persisted progress key.

required.description: Whether revealing this annotation is needed to complete the prompt.

title.description: Short learner-facing title shown with the explanation.

CodeAnnotationAnchor.description: An author-friendly anchor that avoids absolute character offsets.

line.description: 1-based line number the target text occurs on.

occurrence.description: 1-based occurrence of `text` on the line. Defaults to the first.

text.description: Exact text that must occur on that line.

CompleteMissionRequest.description:
Request to complete a mission.

The owner is taken from the verified token, so no identity is required here.

device_id.description: Device/install context. Not an authorization proof.

name.description: Short learner-facing name, for example `CloudFormation change sets`.

ConceptWeight.description: A concept mapped to a question, with its share of the evidence.

weight.description: Share of the question attributed to this concept, in `(0, 1]`.

ConfigSlot.description: A named role the learner assigns a component to.

label.description: Learner-facing label for the role, for example `IPv4 default route target`.

CyberDefenseUpgradeRequest.description:
Request to debit Bits for one Cyber Defense control upgrade.

The client sends only the action's primitives: the server derives the
control's level from its own settled ledger, computes the canonical cost from
policy, and never trusts a client-supplied amount. `event_id` is the
idempotency key, so a retry after a timeout cannot debit twice.

defense_id.description: Control being upgraded. Recorded for audit; it does not affect the cost.

event_id.description: Client-generated idempotency key for this upgrade action.

from_level.description:
Level the client believes it is upgrading from. The server derives the
expected level from the settled ledger and rejects a mismatch.

run_id.description: Client-generated id for the mission attempt the upgrade belongs to.

CyberDefenseUpgradeResponse.description: Outcome of a Cyber Defense upgrade spend.

bits_balance.description: Settled balance after the spend. Unchanged on an idempotent retry.

newly_settled.description: `false` when this `event_id` was already settled (a safe retry).

DailyItemCompleteRequest.description: Request to complete a learning-node Daily Mission item.

discovery.description: Raw Knowledge Map discovery progress used to derive node completion.

DailyItemCompleteResponse.description: Result of completing one Daily Mission item.

item_completed.description: Whether the item is now complete.

DailyMissionItemDto.description: One item of the learner's Daily Mission.

position.description: Zero-based position in the immutable plan.

question_count.description: Number of server-selected questions, for practice items.

DailyMissionItemStatus.description: Completion status of one Daily Mission item.

DailyMissionPlanType.description: How a Daily Mission was generated.

DailyMissionRequest.description: Request for the learner's Daily Mission for today.

discovery.description: Raw Knowledge Map discovery progress, if available.

timezone.description: Client IANA timezone. Stored as metadata; the day boundary is canonical UTC.

DailyMissionResponse.description: The learner's immutable Daily Mission snapshot for the canonical day.

reward_bits.description: Bits bonus for completing the whole mission.

reward_granted.description: Whether the completion bonus has been settled.

DiscoveryResponse.description:
Server-persisted Knowledge Map discovery progress for a learning track.

Discovery is raw and monotonic: node/module state is derived by the client
with the same rules as the Knowledge Map. It is never learning evidence.

track_version.description: Learning track version the progress belongs to.

DiscoveryState.description:
Discovery dimension of the Knowledge Signal.

Whether the learner explored the node's learning content. This is separate
from scored evidence and is never a mastery claim.

DiscoveryUpdateRequest.description:
A monotonic Knowledge Map discovery delta for one track version.

Discovery is set-union based, so duplicates are harmless and an older device
can never remove a newer reveal.

content_version.description: Learning content version the reveals were recorded against.

track_version.description: Learning track version the discovery belongs to.

DomainDiscoveryInput.description: Raw discovery progress for one learning domain, as stored on the client.

revealed_element_ids.description: Knowledge node id to prompt id to revealed discovery element ids.

revealed_prompt_ids.description: Knowledge node id to the prompt ids the learner has revealed.

learning_available.description: Whether pre-quiz learning content exists for this domain.

DomainProgressDto.description: Knowledge Signal for one domain's nodes.

ErrorCodeDef.description: A structured error the scorer may emit for a question.

ErrorResponse.description: Envelope returned for every API error.

EvaluationSliceDto.description: Metrics for one slice of the evaluation set.

key.description: Slice key within the dimension, for example `recall`.

mean_observed.description: Mean observed score for the slice.

mean_prediction.description: Mean predicted probability for the slice.

samples.description: Number of samples in the slice.

EvidenceLevel.description:
Coarse evidence level for a node or one assessment mode.

This is an amount-of-evidence signal, never a mastery claim. A node with
little evidence looks "early", not deficient.

bits_preview.description:
Bits the learner is expected to earn when this attempt is settled.

A preview only: the authoritative balance is settled during sync.

correct.description: Whether the attempt was fully correct.

FillSlot.description: A blank the learner must fill from a constrained option set.

label.description: Learner-facing label for the blank, for example `Destination`.

FixedNode.description: A node that is already provided as part of the scaffold.

position.description: Where the node is shown relative to the slots in `linear` layouts.

x.description: Authored horizontal position for `graph` layouts, in `0..=1`.

y.description: Authored vertical position for `graph` layouts, in `0..=1`.

FixedNodePosition.description: Where a provided node sits relative to a reconstruction's slots.

FreshnessState.description: Coarse freshness signal, used only for the outer ring.

GlossaryTerm.description:
One clickable term in learner-facing text, with its explanation.

Authors list terms here; the app highlights matching occurrences in learning
text and reveals the definition when the learner activates the term.

definition.description: Short learner-facing explanation shown when the term is activated.

term.description: The text to highlight, for example `guest memory`.

HealthResponse.description:
Safe operational health payload. Never includes connection strings, hosts,
versions of dependencies, or other internals.

oneOf.description: Place items into categories.
Arrange items into a meaningful order.
Connect nodes with directed relationships.
Rebuild a structure by placing pieces into a scaffold's slots.

fixed_nodes.description: Nodes already provided as context. Not part of the answer.

oneOf.description: Select the evidence sources relevant to a question.

evidence.description: Candidate telemetry, log, or evidence sources.

oneOf.description: Identify the faulty element(s) in an authored configuration.

elements.description: Structured elements (components, rules, rows) the learner inspects.

oneOf.description: Fill blanks with values drawn from a constrained option set.

options.description: Values the learner may use. May contain distractors.

slots.description: Blanks to fill, in presentation order.

oneOf.description: Follow a deterministic diagnosis/remediation decision tree.
Follow a deterministic authored decision chain.
Assemble a configuration by assigning components to named roles.

pieces.description: Components the learner may assign. May contain distractors.

slots.description: Named roles that each expect one component.

oneOf.description: Place items on a two-axis conceptual map.
Assemble an ordered statement from a token pool.

tokens.description: Tokens the learner may use. May contain distractors.

oneOf.description: Fill inline blanks inside a sentence by typing the missing text.

slots.description: Blanks referenced anywhere in the content, in declaration order.

oneOf.description: Choose exactly one option.
Choose an exact set of options.

required_selections.description: Number of options the learner must select.

oneOf.description:
Write Python that is executed and checked locally in the browser.

Learner source is never sent to the API for execution. The browser runs
it in an isolated runtime and submits only the count of authored tests
that passed; the server re-scores that primitive against the canonical
test list. See `docs/14-security-privacy.md`.

entrypoint.description: Name of the callable under test. Empty for script-style exercises.

language.description: Runtime language. Only `python` is supported initially.

packages.description:
Packages the content explicitly declares from the application
allowlist. Empty for standard-library-only exercises.

Interaction.description: Interaction definition shown to the learner. Contains no answer key.

InteractionType.description: The tactile interaction family a question uses.

IssueMissionRequest.description: Request to issue a mission for a quiz mode.

device_id.description:
Device/install context. Ownership always comes from the authenticated
user; this value is never used as an authorization proof.

domain_id.description: Domain to scope a domain quiz to. Ignored for other modes.

mode.description: Quiz mode deciding how the server selects questions.

module_id.description:
Learning module (section) to scope a section quiz to. Required for
`section_quiz`; ignored for other modes.

question_id.description:
Anchor question for `recommended_practice`. The server validates it
belongs to the certification version; it never trusts it as the whole
practice set.

recommendation_id.description:
Recommendation that produced this mission, when it was recommended.
Context only, never an authorization key.

task_id.description: Task to scope a task practice to. Required for `task_practice`.

KnowledgeNode.description: One knowledge card on the map.

concept_ids.description: Certification concepts this node teaches. The bridge to quiz evidence.

glossary.description:
Clickable terms with short explanations, scoped to this node's page.

Merged with the domain glossary when the card renders; a node term wins
over a domain term with the same text.

map_position.description: Authored position on the map in `0..=1` space.

prerequisite_node_ids.description: Nodes that must be unlocked before this node becomes ready.

prompts.description: Progressive reveal prompts. All required prompts unlock the node.

KnowledgePrompt.description: One progressive-reveal prompt on a knowledge card.

id.description: Stable prompt identifier within the node.

kind.description: Prompt kind, which selects the shared icon and styling vocabulary.

label.description: Learner-facing label, authored by the curriculum.

placeholder.description:
Blank text shown before the reveal. Optional: an empty placeholder
renders a generic `?` blank, and interactive reveals ignore it.

required.description: Whether revealing this prompt counts toward unlocking the node.

reveal.description: The information revealed when the learner taps the blank.

LearningDesign.description: The vocabulary and rules shown to learners on the map.

mastery_note.description: Reminder that discovery is not mastery.

progress_label.description: Label for discovery progress, for example `Discovery Progress`.

LearningDomainMeta.description: Domain identity within a certification blueprint.

LearningDomainResponse.description:
Learner-facing learning content for one certification domain.

This is the discovery layer that sits before retrieval practice. Reveals are
present because progressive disclosure is the mechanic, not a secret. Quiz
canonical answers are never included.

glossary.description: Clickable terms with short explanations, highlighted in learner text.

LearningModule.description: A group of knowledge nodes unlocked along one path.

prerequisite_module_ids.description: Modules that must be completed before this one becomes available.

skill_ids.description: Exam skill ids this module teaches.

task_ids.description: Exam task ids this module teaches.

oneOf.description: A short prose reveal.

Optional progressive reveal configuration. When present, the
sentence is always rendered and only the authored spans inside it
are hidden until the learner reveals each one. When omitted the
whole text is revealed as a unit exactly as before.

text.description: Revealed text. Keep it to one or two sentences.

oneOf.description: An ordered sequence, rendered top-to-bottom with arrows.
A compact set of bullets.
Keyword clues, rendered as compact chips.
A side-by-side or stacked comparison.
A real table: typed column ids with one row per record.

Optional progressive reveal configuration. When omitted the table is
revealed as a whole exactly as before.

rows.description: Table rows. Every row must fill every column.

oneOf.description:
A read-only, syntax-highlighted file with clickable annotations.

The `code` string is the verbatim file. Annotation anchors point into it
by line and text so authors never hand-count character offsets, and the
raw source stays valid and copyable.

code.description: Verbatim file contents. Never marked up or executed.

filename.description: Display filename shown in the header bar.

line_numbers.description: Whether to render a line-number gutter.

LearningReveal.description:
How a revealed prompt renders. Deliberately not a plain string: the
curriculum distinguishes prose, sequences, comparisons, and keyword clues.

MapPosition.description: Normalized position on the knowledge map.

MeResponse.description: Safe application account data for the signed-in learner.

email.description: Email known for the account, when the provider supplied one.

id.description: Internal application user id. The stable ownership key.

streak.description:
Account-wide daily study streak.

Bundled here so the Track Hub does not need a separate streak request.
Best-effort: a streak query failure returns a neutral streak and never
fails authentication.

MissionResponse.description: A server-issued mission with its questions.

module_id.description: Learning module (section) covered, for a section quiz.

questions.description:
Questions in presentation order.

Ordinary study missions intentionally ship their canonical scoring data
so they can be scored locally with zero per-question requests. The server
still re-scores every raw answer during `/v1/sync`; the client score is
never authoritative. Practice tests keep the answer-key-free
[`QuestionView`].

MissionReviewResponse.description:
Read-only review of a completed mission.

Lets a learner revisit the questions and answers of completed work without
redoing it. It is never learning evidence.

questions.description: Questions in presentation order, with canonical answers.

ModeSignal.description: One assessment mode's signal for a node.

freshness_state.description: Freshness of the evidence in this mode.

ModelEvaluationResponse.description:
Internal calibration summary for one model version.

Analytics only: no per-user data is exposed.

slices.description:
Metrics sliced by assessment mode, source, track, domain, difficulty,
spacing, and delayed-retrieval flag.

Node.description: A node in a connection graph.

x.description: Horizontal position in an abstract `0..=1` layout space.

y.description: Vertical position in an abstract `0..=1` layout space.

NodeProgressDto.description: Knowledge Signal for one knowledge node.

discovery_state.description: Whether the learner explored the node's content.

evidence_level.description: Amount of scored evidence (coarse; never a percentage).

freshness_state.description: Freshness of that evidence (outer-ring treatment only).

mode_signals.description: Per-assessment-mode signals, present only for modes with evidence.

PedagogyMetadata.description:
Optional, track-agnostic pedagogical metadata authored on a question.

Every field is optional, so existing content without `pedagogy` keeps
loading unchanged. The metadata is descriptive in Phase 1: it is stored in
canonical content and exposed to server-side planning, but it never changes
mastery, scoring, rewards, or selection ranking.

The `*_id` and `surface_context` values are opaque, author-defined strings.
Core code must never branch on their contents, and no global enum exists for
them, so any current or future track (DSA, Python, AWS, Terraform, security,
ML) can use the same contract.

challenge_group_id.description:
Groups questions that may eventually form one multi-stage learning
journey. Phase 1 stores the grouping only; it does not sequence it.

family_id.description:
Deeper reusable family/pattern/strategy/conceptual structure this
activity belongs to, for example `dsa.sliding_window.variable`.

scaffold_level.description:
How much assistance is embedded in the activity, `0..=6`.

This is not difficulty: an easy question may embed no help and a hard
question may embed substantial help. It never modifies
`difficulty_prior`.

oneOf.description: Instructional role of this particular activity.

transfer_group_id.description: Groups activities that exercise the same deep transferable structure.

PedagogyStage.description:
The instructional role an authored activity plays.

This is deliberately separate from [`AssessmentMode`]: an assessment mode
describes the *evidence* an attempt provides, while a pedagogy stage
describes *what the learner is being asked to do* in the activity. The
values are domain-neutral; track-specific structure belongs in authored
`family_id`/`transfer_group_id`/`challenge_group_id` strings, never here.

Phase 1 is descriptive only. The stage is stored and exposed to server-side
planning code, but does not yet change selection or mastery.

PlacementAxis.description: One axis of a two-dimensional conceptual map.

high_label.description: Label for the high end of the axis.

low_label.description: Label for the low end of the axis.

PlacementPoint.description: A point submitted for a two-dimensional placement.

PlacementRegion.description: A tolerant canonical region on a two-dimensional map.

PlannerAction.description: A next action the learner can take.

PracticeTestAnswerRequest.description: The learner's answer to one practice-test item.

answer.description: Answer primitives, keyed by the question's interaction type.

PracticeTestDomainResult.description: Scored accuracy for one exam domain, over scored items only.

correct.description: Scored items answered correctly in this domain.

PracticeTestItemResult.description: One reviewed practice-test item, available only after submission.

answered.description: Whether the learner submitted any answer.

canonical_answer.description: Canonical answer, safe to reveal after submission.

choice_feedback.description: Per-choice feedback keyed by choice id, safe after submission.

correct.description: Whether the submission was fully correct; `None` when unanswered.

interaction.description: Interaction definition, used to render labels in review.

is_scored.description: Whether the item counts toward the practice score.

oneOf.description: The learner's submitted answer, when any.

PracticeTestItemView.description:
One learner-safe practice-test item, before submission.

No answer key, per-choice feedback, or scored flag is present.

question.description: The question to present, in authored order.

PracticeTestListResponse.description: Practice tests available for one certification.

PracticeTestResponse.description: Learner-safe practice-test content served before submission.

scored_question_count.description: Items that count toward the practice score.

PracticeTestResultResponse.description: Full practice-test result and review, available only after submission.

domain_breakdown.description: Per-domain scored accuracy, derived from authored content.

raw_accuracy.description: Raw accuracy across scored items, in `[0, 1]`.

score_note.description: Explicit note that this raw score is not an official scaled score.

scored_question_count.description: Items that count toward the practice score.

PracticeTestSubmissionRequest.description:
One-shot submission of a practice-test attempt.

Answers are keyed by question id; unanswered items are simply omitted.

answers.description: Submitted answers, at most one per question.

PracticeTestSummaryDto.description:
Summary of one available practice test (exam simulation).

Metadata only: it never contains questions or answers. The scored count is
an aggregate and does not reveal which items are unscored.

scored_question_count.description: Items that count toward the practice score.

PromptKind.description:
The shared prompt vocabulary. Icons are selected by the UI from this kind,
so content can change labels without the renderer special-casing nodes.

PythonCodeAnswer.description:
Browser-executed Python result primitives.

The learner's source never reaches the API. The client runs the authored
tests locally and reports only how many passed; the server re-scores those
counts against the canonical test list.

passed.description: Number of authored tests the learner's program passed.

total.description: Total tests executed. Must equal the question's authored test count.

oneOf.description:
Call the entrypoint with positional arguments and compare the returned
value for equality.

expected.description: Expected return value as a JSON value.

oneOf.description: Call the entrypoint and require it to raise a named exception.

exception.description: Expected exception class name, for example `ValueError`.

oneOf.description: Compare the program's captured standard output.

expected.description: Expected standard output, compared after trimming trailing newlines.

PythonTest.description:
One data-driven assertion in a browser-executed Python exercise.

Tests are trusted authored content, never learner input. They ship to the
browser so the learner's program can be executed and checked locally, which
means they are inspectable rather than secret. Expected values are passed as
structured JSON data: they are never interpolated into generated Python
source and never evaluated by the server.

QuestionView.description: A question shown to the learner. Contains no answer key.

instruction.description:
Optional authored instruction shown with the prompt, for example
`Choose TWO.`. Never reveals the answer.

QuizMode.description:
The quiz mode a mission was issued for.

`task_practice` is kept for the demo/task flow and internal debugging; the
learner-facing modes are quick, domain, full practice, and the one-question
section quiz that concludes a learning module.

oneOf.description: Assessment mode the recommendation is measured in, when known.

node_id.description: Knowledge node to open, when the action is node-based.

node_title.description: Learner-facing node title, when the action is node-based.

question_id.description: Question to practice, when the action targets one.

title.description: Short learner-facing title, for example `Learn tensor broadcasting`.

track_id.description: Learning track the recommendation belongs to.

oneOf.description: Planner action the recommendation had, when known.

event_id.description:
Stable client-generated id for idempotent retries. Generated by the
server when absent.

RecommendationEventResponse.description:
Result of recording a lifecycle event.

`recorded` is `false` when the auxiliary write failed; the request still
succeeds because telemetry must never block learning.

RecommendationReason.description: A stable, explainable reason code for a recommendation.

RecommendationRequest.description:
Request body for a recommendation.

Discovery progress is optional and best-effort: it lets the planner mirror
the Knowledge Map's exact unlock semantics. It is never learning evidence.

discovery.description: Raw Knowledge Map discovery progress for the track, if available.

RecommendationResponse.description:
Best-effort next-action recommendation for a learning track.

Recommendations are optional and explainable. `recommendation` is `null` when
the track has nothing actionable yet, and the field is never required for the
dashboard to render.

oneOf.description: The chosen recommendation, or `null` when none is available.

recommendation_id.description:
Stable id for this recommendation, used by lifecycle telemetry. `null`
only when no recommendation was produced.

edges.description: Directed `[from, to]` relationships the learner drew.

placements.description: Slot id to piece id placements.

ReconstructionLayout.description: How a reconstruction scaffold represents structure.

ReconstructionSlot.description: A structural position the learner fills with a piece.

x.description: Authored horizontal position for `graph` layouts, in `0..=1`.

y.description: Authored vertical position for `graph` layouts, in `0..=1`.

RevealColumn.description: One titled column of a comparison reveal.

RevealTableColumn.description: One column of a table reveal.

id.description: Stable identifier used to key every row's cells.

RevealTableRow.description: One row of a table reveal.

cells.description: Column id to cell text. Every authored column must be present.

id.description:
Stable row identifier. Optional so existing static tables stay valid,
but required by progressive row and cell reveals.

ReviewedAttempt.description: One accepted attempt in a read-only mission review.

correct.description: Whether the attempt cleared the success threshold.

canonical_answer.description: Canonical answer, safe to show after completion.

interaction.description: Interaction definition, used to render labels in review.

ScenarioStep.description: One authored decision point in a branching scenario.

next_step_by_choice.description: Choice id to next step id. A choice with no entry ends the scenario.

stage.description: What kind of decision this step represents.

node_title.description: Learner-facing node title, for node activities.

question_ids.description:
Server-selected questions, for `practice` activities. The client never
supplies these; it only anchors the mission on the first one.

title.description: Short learner-facing title, for example `Review VPC route tables`.

SessionActivityKind.description: What one session activity asks the learner to do.

SessionPreference.description: How the learner wants a session balanced.

SourceRef.description: A reference to the official source of a content unit.

StreakDto.description:
Account-wide daily study streak.

Motivational only: it never feeds concept state, scoring, or rewards. It
spans every learning track.

active_today.description: Whether today is already a qualified study day.

current.description: Consecutive active days ending today or yesterday.

last_active_day.description: Most recent qualified local day, `YYYY-MM-DD`, when any.

StudyQuestionView.description:
A question for an ordinary study mission that supports local scoring.

This is the only mission-facing DTO that carries canonical answers. It keeps
every learner-facing field of [`QuestionView`] and adds the deterministic
scoring metadata needed to score an attempt in the browser.

The extra fields are explicitly *not* authoritative: `/v1/sync` always
re-scores the raw submitted answer against the server-known content before
accepting evidence, settling Bits, or updating concept state. Practice tests
and any pre-submit response keep using [`QuestionView`], which never exposes
an answer key.

canonical_answer.description: Canonical answer, used for local scoring and immediate feedback.

choice_feedback.description: Per-choice feedback keyed by choice id.

error_codes.description: Authored structured error-code definitions for this question.

instruction.description:
Optional authored instruction shown with the prompt, for example
`Choose TWO.`. Never reveals the answer.

track_id.description: Learning track the session belongs to.

StudySessionRequest.description:
Request body for an adaptive study session.

Session planning is optional; a failed request never blocks the dashboard.

available_minutes.description: Requested approximate session length in minutes. Clamped to a sane range.

discovery.description: Raw Knowledge Map discovery progress for the track, if available.

preference.description: How to balance learning and retrieval practice.

activities.description:
Ordered activities. Empty when nothing is actionable; the client then
builds a standard non-adaptive session.

session_id.description: Stable id for this session, used by auxiliary telemetry.

track_id.description: Learning track the session belongs to.

SyncEventRequest.description: One attempt in a sync batch.

content_version.description: Content version the answer was produced against.

SyncEventResult.description:
Result for one synced event.

The server re-scores every raw answer from canonical content, so this is the
authoritative outcome. The client compares it with its optimistic local score
and reconciles any difference (the server always wins).

accepted.description: Whether the event is now accepted server-side.

bits_settled.description: Bits settled for this event (0 when rejected or already settled).

correct.description: Authoritative correctness verdict. `false` for rejected events.

error_codes.description: Authoritative structured error codes. Empty for rejected events.

score.description: Authoritative partial score in `[0, 1]`. `0` for rejected events.

SyncRequest.description:
Request to sync a batch of evaluated attempts.

The request may also carry optional auxiliary sections. They share one HTTP
request to reduce chatter, but their transactional semantics are isolated:
an auxiliary failure never rejects or rolls back accepted learning events.

auxiliary_events.description:
Optional recommendation lifecycle telemetry. Never authoritative.

Deserialized leniently for the same reason as `discovery_updates`.

device_id.description: Device/install context. Ownership comes from the authenticated user.

discovery_updates.description:
Optional Knowledge Map discovery deltas. Never learning evidence.

Deserialized leniently: a malformed entry is dropped rather than failing
the whole request, so it can never block accepted learning events.

events.description: Attempts to reconcile. Strict: authoritative events must be well-formed.

timezone.description:
Client IANA timezone. Captured once if absent so the account-wide study
streak uses the learner's local day boundary, matching Daily Missions.

auxiliary.description: Disposition of the optional auxiliary telemetry section.

bits_balance.description: Authoritative settled Bits balance after this batch.

discovery.description: Disposition of the optional discovery section.

SyncSectionResult.description:
Disposition of one optional sync section.

`accepted` is `false` when the auxiliary work failed; the request still
succeeds and the client only retains the failed section for retry.

TableInitialVisibility.description:
Information that is visible before the learner reveals anything.

A cell is initially visible when its column, its row, or its derived cell id
(`row_id:column_id`) is listed. The three lists combine, so authors can give
away a column, an entire row, and one extra cell in one table.

column_ids.description: Column ids whose cells are all visible from the start.

row_ids.description: Row ids whose cells are all visible from the start.

TableProgressiveReveal.description:
Progressive reveal configuration for a `table` reveal.

The table itself is always rendered immediately. Discovery is limited to the
reveal units selected by `mode`, minus anything already exposed through
`initially_visible`.

initially_visible.description: Information shown from the beginning, before any reveal.

mode.description: Whether the learner reveals whole rows, whole columns, or single cells.

TableRevealMode.description: The unit a learner reveals in a progressive table.

TaskDto.description: A task with a count of authored questions.

TextProgressiveReveal.description:
Progressive reveal configuration for a `text` reveal.

The sentence is always rendered in full. Discovery is limited to the
authored `spans` inside it: each span is replaced by an inline reveal
control until the learner activates it.

spans.description: Hidden words or phrases inside the reveal text, in any order.

TextRevealSpan.description:
One hidden word or phrase inside a progressive `text` reveal.

Span text may contain multiple words. It is located inside the parent
sentence by exact text plus an optional occurrence, so repeated wording is
disambiguated the same way code annotation anchors are.

id.description: Stable span identifier, also the persisted progress key.

occurrence.description: 1-based occurrence of `text` in the sentence. Defaults to the first.

required.description: Whether revealing this span is needed to complete the prompt.

text.description: Exact authored text to hide. May contain multiple words.

TrackMapResponse.description:
All learner-facing learning content for one learning track.

This is a read-only aggregate over authored content so the Track Hub can
render one track-wide Knowledge Map without a request per domain. It carries
no scored answers and no learner state.

domains.description: Learning domains with modules, nodes, and reveals.

TrackProgressResponse.description:
Aggregate Knowledge Signal for one learning track.

One request returns every domain and node so the Track Hub never fetches
per-node state. Coarse semantic states only: no raw model probabilities,
percentages, or pass estimates.

TypedBlankAnswer.description:
Accepted typed answers for one blank.

Matching is deterministic: the normalized typed answer must equal one of the
explicitly authored aliases. There is no semantic or fuzzy matching.

accepted_answers.description: Authored answers that are accepted for this blank.

TypedBlankSlot.description:
A blank the learner fills by typing free text.

The slot's `id` is referenced as `{{id}}` inside a content template.

The optional presentation hints (`width_chars`, `multiline`, `rows`) only
shape the input; they never affect scoring or the accepted answers.

id.description: Stable identifier within the question, used as the `{{id}}` placeholder.

label.description: Learner-facing label for the blank, for example `Policy result`.

multiline.description: Whether the blank should render as a multi-line answer box.

placeholder.description: Optional hint text shown inside the empty input.

rows.description:
Optional number of visible rows for a multi-line blank. Only meaningful
when `multiline` is true.

width_chars.description:
Optional initial/minimum visible width of the blank, in characters.

When omitted the input keeps its historical auto-growing behavior.

oneOf.description: A sentence or short prose statement containing `{{slot_id}}` placeholders.
A syntax-highlighted source-code sample containing `{{slot_id}}` placeholders.

template.description:
Code template containing `{{slot_id}}` placeholders. Newlines and
indentation are significant.

oneOf.description: A table whose cells may contain text or code templates.

TypedFillContent.description:
Presentation context for a typed fill-in-the-blank interaction.

Presentation is explicit and tagged, so the renderer never has to guess
whether authored content is prose, source code, or a table. Blank positions
are always marked with `{{slot_id}}` inside a `template`.

oneOf.description: A text template containing `{{slot_id}}` placeholders.
A syntax-highlighted code template containing `{{slot_id}}` placeholders.

TypedFillTableCell.description: Presentation of one typed fill-in-the-blank table cell.

TypedFillTableColumn.description: A column in a typed fill-in-the-blank table.

TypedFillTableRow.description: A row in a typed fill-in-the-blank table.

cells.description: Column id to the cell presented in that column.

UpdateSettingsRequest.description: Request to update learner study settings.

unlock_all_materials.description: Whether all study materials should be unlocked.

Whether the learner unlocks all study materials instead of the guided,
in-order path. A preference only; it never affects scoring or evidence.

WalletResponse.description:
A learner's settled Bits balance.

The wallet is owned by the authenticated user, so it is read from the token
rather than from a client-supplied identifier.
